From Wiktionary, the free dictionary
See also: Pilar, pilař, and Pilař

English

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

Learned borrowing from Latin pilāris, from Latin pilus (“a hair”) +‎ -ar.

Adjective

[edit]

pilar (not comparable)

  1. (chiefly medicine) Relating to hair.
    pilar muscle; pilar cyst
  2. Covered in hair; hairy.

Anagrams

[edit]
  • Paril, April, prial, Plair

Catalan

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

Inherited from Vulgar Latin *pīlāre, from Latin pīla (“pillar”).

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): (Central, Balearic) [piˈla]
  • IPA(key): (Valencia) [piˈlaɾ]

Noun

[edit]

pilar m (plural pilars)

  1. pillar
  2. (castells) a castell built with just one casteller on each level
  3. (castells) each of the vertical columns of castellers making up the tronc of a castell (syn. rengla)

Derived terms

[edit]
  • pilar caminant
  • pilar de dol

Further reading

[edit]
  • “pilar”, in Diccionari de la llengua catalana [Dictionary of the Catalan Language] (in Catalan), second edition, Institute of Catalan Studies [Catalan: Institut d'Estudis Catalans], April 2007
  • “pilar”, in Gran Diccionari de la Llengua Catalana, Grup Enciclopèdia Catalana, 2026
  • “pilar” in Diccionari normatiu valencià, Acadèmia Valenciana de la Llengua.
  • Alcover, Antoni Maria; Moll, Francesc de Borja (1963), “pilar”, in Diccionari català-valencià-balear (in Catalan)

Indonesian

[edit]
Indonesian Wikipedia has an article on:
pilar
Wikipedia id

Etymology

[edit]

From Dutch pilaar, from Medieval Latin pīlāre, from Latin pīla (“a pillar”).

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • (Standard Indonesian) IPA(key): /ˈpilar/ [ˈpi.lar]
  • Rhymes: -ilar
  • Syllabification: pi‧lar

Noun

[edit]

pilar (plural pilar-pilar)

  1. pillar:
    1. (architecture) a large post, often used as supporting architecture
    2. (figurative) an essential part of something that provides support
      Synonyms: dasar, induk
  2. (nautical) mast: a tall, slim post or tower, usually tapering upward, used to support, for example, the sails on a ship, flags, floodlights, meteorological instruments, or communications equipment such as an aerial, usually supported by guy-wires

Affixed terms

[edit]
  • berpilar

Further reading

[edit]
  • “pilar”, in Kamus Besar Bahasa Indonesia [Great Dictionary of the Indonesian Language] (in Indonesian), Jakarta: Agency for Language Development and Cultivation – Ministry of Education, Culture, Research, and Technology of the Republic of Indonesia, 2016

Norwegian Bokmål

[edit]
Norwegian Wikipedia has an article on:
pilar
Wikipedia no

Etymology

[edit]

From Latin pīlāre, from Latin pīla (“a pillar”). Either inherited from Old Norse (compare Icelandic pílári) or a later borrowing.

Noun

[edit]

pilar m (definite singular pilaren, indefinite plural pilarer, definite plural pilarene)

  1. a pillar, column
  2. a pier (of a bridge)

Derived terms

[edit]
  • grunnpilar

References

[edit]
  • “pilar” in The Bokmål Dictionary.

pilar f or m

  1. indefinite masculine plural of pil

Etymology 2

[edit]

From Latin pīlāre, from Latin pīla (“a pillar”). Either inherited from Old Norse (compare Icelandic pílári) or a later borrowing.

Noun

[edit]

pilar m (definite singular pilaren, indefinite plural pilarar, definite plural pilarane)

  1. a pillar, column
  2. a pier (of a bridge)

Etymology 1

[edit]

Inherited from Vulgar Latin *pīlāre, from Latin pīla (“pillar”).

Noun

[edit]

pilar m (plural pilars)

  1. pillar

Etymology 2

[edit]

From Old Occitan, inherited from Latin pīlāre (“to grind, pound”).

Verb

[edit]

pilar

  1. to crush; to pulverize

Portuguese

[edit]

Etymology 1

[edit]

Inherited from Vulgar Latin *pīlāre, from Latin pīla (“pillar”).

Alternative forms

[edit]
  • pillar (pre-reform spelling)

Pronunciation

[edit]
 
  • (Brazil) IPA(key): /piˈlaʁ/ [piˈlah]
  • (Brazil) IPA(key): /piˈlaʁ/ [piˈlah]
    • (São Paulo) IPA(key): /piˈlaɾ/
    • (Rio de Janeiro) IPA(key): /piˈlaʁ/ [piˈlaχ]
    • (Caipira) IPA(key): /piˈlaɻ/
 
  • (Portugal) IPA(key): /piˈlaɾ/
  • (Portugal) IPA(key): /piˈlaɾ/
    • (Southern Portugal) IPA(key): /piˈla.ɾi/

  • Homophone: pilhar (Madeira)
  • Hyphenation: pi‧lar

Noun

[edit]

pilar m (plural pilares)

  1. pillar (large post, often used as supporting architecture)
  2. (figurative) pillar (essential part of something)

Etymology 2

[edit]

Inherited from Latin pīlāre (“to grind, pound”). By surface analysis, pilão (“pestle”) +‎ -ar.

Pronunciation

[edit]
 
  • (Brazil) IPA(key): /piˈla(ʁ)/ [piˈla(h)]
  • (Brazil) IPA(key): /piˈla(ʁ)/ [piˈla(h)]
    • (São Paulo) IPA(key): /piˈla(ɾ)/
    • (Rio de Janeiro) IPA(key): /piˈla(ʁ)/ [piˈla(χ)]
    • (Caipira) IPA(key): /piˈla(ɻ)/
 
  • (Portugal) IPA(key): /piˈlaɾ/
  • (Portugal) IPA(key): /piˈlaɾ/
    • (Southern Portugal) IPA(key): /piˈla.ɾi/

  • Homophone: pilhar (Madeira)
  • Hyphenation: pi‧lar

Verb

[edit]

pilar (first-person singular present pilo, first-person singular preterite pilei, past participle pilado)

  1. to grind using a pestle

Spanish

[edit]

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /piˈlaɾ/ [piˈlaɾ]
  • Rhymes: -aɾ
  • Syllabification: pi‧lar

Etymology 1

[edit]

Inherited from Vulgar Latin *pīlāre, from Latin pīla (“pillar”).

Noun

[edit]

pilar m (plural pilares)

  1. pillar, pier, mainstay
  2. (rugby) prop (the player who is next to the hooker in a scrum)
Derived terms
[edit]
  • Pilar f (name)

Etymology 2

[edit]

Inherited from Latin pīlāre (“to grind, pound”).

Verb

[edit]

pilar (first-person singular present pilo, first-person singular preterite pilé, past participle pilado)

  1. to pound
